sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997)
sources.locator: Complete PDF retrieved. Read Chapter 3, tetrads and non-coordinate bases, printed pp. 88–95 (PDF pp. 95–102), equations (3.114)–(3.144). This covers orthonormal coframes, local Lorentz changes, connection transformation, Cartan torsion/curvature forms, both Bianchi equations, and the metric-compatibility condition.

contents.name: Equations (3.114)–(3.126): tetrads, dual coframes, metric reconstruction, and pointwise Lorentz changes
contents.support: The tetrad and coframe definition records the (-+++) convention and local Lorentz change. The frame-bundle proposition proves local oriented, future-directed frame sections and the SO+(1,3) action.

contents.name: Equations (3.128)–(3.134): orthonormal-frame covariant derivatives and inhomogeneous spin-connection law
contents.support: The definition states the connection matrix convention and derives the change law with e'=Lambda e and omega'=Lambda omega Lambda^-1-dLambda Lambda^-1.

contents.name: Equations (3.137)–(3.139): Cartan torsion form and equality with tangent-bundle torsion components
contents.support: Step 1.1 evaluates the exterior derivative and wedge terms on X,Y and identifies T^I(X,Y) with the coframe component of nabla_XY-nabla_YX-[X,Y].

contents.name: Equations (3.138) and (3.143): curvature two-form and eta-skew metric-compatible connection
contents.support: The definition fixes F=domega+omega wedge omega and defines Lorentz connections by omega_IJ=-omega_JI.

contents.name: Equation (3.141): second Bianchi identity for a bundle connection
contents.support: The definition remarks that the local curvature satisfies this identity by the cited published bundle-connection theorem; the assigned pair does not duplicate its proof.

contents.name: Equation (3.140): first Cartan Bianchi identity relating D T and F wedge e
contents.reason: The assigned claims need torsion-curvature definitions and the second Bianchi identity only; this additional identity is neither a prerequisite nor a planned assertion, and it can be developed separately if a later result uses it.

contents.name: Equation (3.144): component solution of the torsion equation for omega
contents.reason: The equivalence item proves existence and uniqueness by constructing the Levi-Civita connection in the tetrad, so a closed component formula is not needed to establish any assigned claim.

sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.4.2 Connection 1-forms and Curvature 2-forms
sources.locator: §3.4.2, HTML lines 1133–1243; read the complete section on connection one-forms, curvature, torsion, and the structure equations.

contents.name: Connection one-forms in an orthonormal frame
contents.support: The A definition fixes the induced affine connection and its matrix entries in a local tetrad, including the eta-skew metric-compatibility condition.

contents.name: Curvature two-form and local gauge transformation
contents.support: The definition gives the matrix-valued curvature form; step 4.1 of the torsion equivalence proposition expands and verifies its Lorentz gauge covariance.

contents.name: Torsion two-form and its relation to affine torsion
contents.support: Step 1.1 proves the local component identity and both directions of the zero-torsion equivalence.

contents.name: Curvature structure equation and second Bianchi identity
contents.support: The current definition cites the published bundle-connection curvature and second-Bianchi interface; no duplicate theorem is added.

sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.5.6 Spinors
sources.locator: §4.5.6, HTML lines 1252–1321; read the complete spinor section, including the Lorentzian spin group and local spinor derivative conventions. This is the same independent treatment as the Tong §3.4.2 entry above, not an additional independent source.

contents.name: Lorentzian spin representations and local spinor bundle interface
contents.support: The spin-lift definition uses SL(2,C), a supplied equivariant double cover of the oriented time-oriented frame bundle, and associated bundles for supplied representations.

contents.name: Gamma matrices and the spin covariant derivative
contents.support: The proposition states the gamma anticommutator and proves the commutator identity and compatibility of D=d+(1/4)omega_IJ gamma^I gamma^J with vector Clifford multiplication.

contents.name: Compact SU(2) time-gauge reduction
contents.reason: No time-gauge or reduction choice is supplied in the assigned general Lorentz interface, so no SU(2) representation is substituted for the noncompact Lorentz group.

sources.title: Blagoje Oblak, From the Lorentz Group to the Celestial Sphere, arXiv:1508.00920 (2015)
sources.locator: Complete 45-page PDF retrieved. Read §§2.3.1–2.3.3, PDF pp. 24–27, including the SL(2,C) connectedness proof, Hermitian-matrix Lorentz action, image/kernel computation, and explicit rotations and boosts.

contents.name: §2.3.1 connectedness of SL(2,C)
contents.support: The local lemma gives an explicit QR factorization into SU(2) and an upper-triangular positive-diagonal factor, then contracts both factors by paths.

contents.name: §2.3.2 Hermitian two-by-two matrices and determinant-preserving Lorentz action
contents.support: The proposition defines Pauli matrices and X(x), computes -det X as the (-+++) Minkowski quadratic form, and proves the induced action is Lorentzian.

contents.name: §2.3.2 surjectivity, kernel, and the SL(2,C) double cover
contents.support: The local proof computes kernel {+I,-I}; surjectivity is established by a differential isomorphism, the inverse-function theorem, and connectedness of SO+(1,3), following the assigned design proof route.

contents.name: §2.3.3 explicit spatial-rotation and boost matrices
contents.support: The first B example verifies the z-axis rotation lift A(theta)=exp(-i theta sigma_3/2); the companion boost example verifies the corresponding SL(2,C) boost matrix.

contents.name: The simply-connectedness and universal-cover strengthening
contents.reason: The assigned interface requires a two-sheeted covering homomorphism only; no fundamental-group or universal-cover claim is needed or imported into the local spin structure definition.
